chunks: My father (peace be upon him) and ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Abū al-Qāsim Hārūn ibn Muslim ibn Sa’dān, from Mas‘adah ibn Sadaqah, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for one who goes to the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'A Ḥajj with the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) will be registered for him.' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! A Ḥajj with the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family)?!' He said, 'Yes, and two Ḥajj.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Two Ḥajj?' He said, 'Yes, and three.' He kept increasing the number until he reached ten. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Ten Ḥajj with the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family)?!' He said, 'Yes, and twenty Ḥajj.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Even twenty?' He kept increasing the number until he reached fifty, and then I fell silent.

key_terms.فِدَاكَ: may I be sacrificed for you (a phrase of deep respect)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husain (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith illustrates the Shia concept of *thawab* (reward) multiplication, where the spiritual merit of visiting Imam al-Husayn’s shrine is equated to performing Hajj with the Prophet Muhammad. The progressive enumeration up to fifty times underscores the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia theology, positioning their graves as focal points for divine grace and spiritual elevation comparable to the Prophet himself.
